description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för projektet är att förbättra och utveckla en rad PCAsia-aktiviteter relaterade till kapacitetsutvecklingen av ASEAN:s interparlamentariska församlings (AIPA) medlemsparlament om parlamentariskt arbete. Detta bidrar också till en förbättring av parlamentens prestationer i Sydostasien genom att bidra till att stärka kapaciteten hos parlamentarisk personal och genom att öka intensiteten i tekniskt utbyte och erfarenhetsutbyte mellan deras regionala och internationella kamrater.

The overall objective of the Project is to improve and develop a range of PCAsia activities related to the capacity development of the ASEAN Inter-parliamentary Assembly (AIPA) Member Parliaments on parliamentary works. This also contributes to an improvement in the performance of the Parliaments in South East Asia by helping to strengthen the capacity of parliamentary staff, and by increasing the intensity of technical exchanges and experience-sharing among their regional and international peers.

It is aimed that by 2030, PCAsia contributes to an improvement in the performance of the target Parliaments Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar (currently suspended) and ASEAN Inter- Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA)- by helping to strengthen the capacity of parliamentary staff, and by increasing the intensity of technical exchanges and experience-sharing among their regional peers. There are three indicators as follow: 1) Parliamentary staff provide more effective support to Parliamentarians to perform legislative review, representation and oversight. 2) Parliamentarians perform their core functions of legislation, representation and oversight more effectively. 3) Stakeholders are increasingly satisfied with parliamentary performance.

Examples of outputs that should be highlighted include:
Achieved output by number: From 2023 to 2024, PCAsia delivered 36 capacity development activities in response to requests from ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA) Member Parliaments, involving 1,134 participants (405 women). These activities included core training programmes on Parliamentary Research (91 research products produced), Parliamentary Diplomacy, and Fiscal Analysis, built around peer learning, coaching and practical application.
Institutionalisation of CSO and Expert Input into Lawmaking: throughout 2023 and 2024, PCAsia facilitated the inclusion of civil society perspectives and expertise into the policymaking processes of AIPA Member Parliaments. In Cambodia, input from over ten local CSOs informed parliamentary debate and legislative drafting on the updated Fisheries Law, particularly in areas concerning mangrove protection and small-scale fisheries. These contributions helped Members of Parliament assess the laws provisions through the lens of community livelihoods and environmental sustainability. Similar processes in Laos addressed tobacco control and licensing regulations, drawing on evidence from health-focused CSOs and academic institutions. This integration of grassroots perspectives into formal policy cycles enhanced a more inclusive policy making process.
Public Health Reform Catalysed by Regional Multi-stakeholder Consultation The regional consultation on Methods to Prevent Non-Communicable Diseases and Measures to Reduce Gender Disparity brought together parliamentarians, experts, and civil society organisations (CSOs), helped trigger national policy action in Cambodia. Following the workshop, the country's Ministry of Information issued a directive banning alcohol advertisements that offer rewards or prizes and mandated public health warnings across all platforms. Provincial governments followed suit, further implementing these directives by removing alcohol-related billboards from major roadways. This case illustrates the power of regionally-facilitated, multi-stakeholder dialogue including CSOs to influence domestic policy.
AIPA Resolutions Anchored in PCAsia-Facilitated Regional Dialogue: PCAsia's collaboration with AIPA has directly contributed to the development and adoption of two landmark AIPA Resolutions: Res.43GA/2022/Org/11 and Res.45GA/2024/Soc/03. These resolutions emerged from PCAsia's 2022 regional workshop on The Role of Parliaments in Promoting Inclusive and Sustainable Responses to Health Emergencies, which examined COVID-19 response effectiveness and institutional barriers across the region. Both resolutions call for the institutionalisation of an annual consultative working group between parliaments and civil society within AIPA procedures, aimed at strengthening transparency, data sharing, and preparedness for future health emergencies.
Development of Regional Ethics Guidelines: PCAsia supported the drafting of a regional Parliamentary Codes of Conduct Guidelines from late 2023 to early 2024, with AIPA Member Parliaments to enhance ethical governance, transparency, and integrity. The guidelines were based on requests from the 2023 regional Workshop on Good Governance Practices co-hosted with the Thai Senate, and developed through consultations with MPs and CSOs from five ASEAN countries with the aim to strengthen internal accountability mechanisms in line with international standards. In 2025, PCAsia will convene a regional workshop to present the guidelines to ASEAN parliaments for further input and to support planning toward national-level adaptation.
Parliamentary Ownership and Replication: In 2024, PCAsia alumni independently conducted three national trainings reaching 82 participants. Delivered without external facilitation, this demonstrates effective skill transfer and growing parliamentary confidence to lead internal capacity building activities. It also reduces reliance on international assistance.
Shared Financing and Commitment: the examples included the Indonesian Parliament co-financed PCAsias 2024 Macroeconomic-Budget Model Training (MacBud). Lao PDR and Vietnam also co-sponsored consultations on 2024 AIPA resolution calling for CSOParliamentary information-sharing working groups. Based on this, PCAsia aims to consult with AIPA to explore regional cost-sharing models for cross-parliamentary training programs in the future. This underlines the principle of shared responsibility for regional exchange among member countries.
Mainstreaming Gender Equality and a Human Rights-based Approach: out of 36 capacity development activities conducted during the period, nearly half reached gender balance among participants. In total, 465 women participated across all PCAsia activities - representing 48% of the overall participant pool. Gender equality was integrated into multiple training modules. These included parliamentary research and analysis sessions in parliamentary research and parliamentary diplomacy trainings. For example, the fiscal oversight courses included exercises on assessing the gender impacts of debt-financed infrastructure and how budget allocations affect services used predominantly by women. In the climate finance module, participants examined how environmental taxation and adaptation investments intersect with gender vulnerability and livelihoods.
PCAsia also reinforced gender inclusion through its engagement with parliamentary caucuses and networks. Technical support was provided to the Cambodian Women Parliamentarians Caucus (CWPC), including background research and coordination for communication/outreach activities and women-led public forums. PCAsia additionally contributed to the Women Parliamentarians of AIPA (WAIPA) by facilitating technical input and background briefings for a resolution titled Promoting Women's Political Participation and Leadership for a Sustainable Future, adopted at the 44th AIPA General Assembly in Jakarta in 2023.
PCAsia applied a human rights-based approach through its support for civil society participation in parliamentary processes and multi-stakeholder dialogue. See Institutionalisation of CSO and Expert Input into Lawmaking as above for more information.
Mainstreaming Environment and Climate Change: During 2023 and 2024, climate-related themes were integrated into PCAsia's core training programmes on Parliamentary Research and Parliamentary Diplomacy. In the diplomacy training, country position papers included a focus on climate issues that aligned with the 2024 AIPA General Assembly theme. This helped promote a shared understanding of climate priorities across AIPA Member Parliaments. Climate was also embedded in PCAsia's parliamentary research training. In 2023, research exercises addressed issues such as forest resource governance, climate vulnerability in agricultural zones, and regional environmental cooperation. These activities introduced learners to tools for assessing policy impacts and legislative responses to environmental and climate risks, laying the groundwork for more harmonised approaches across the region.
In addition, PCAsia partnered with UNDP to contribute to the Capacity Development Programme on Climate Change Integration into Planning and Budgeting. This collaboration supported the Cambodian Ministry of Economy and Finance and General Secretariat of the National Council for Sustainable Development (GSSD) in enhancing institutional knowledge on climate change and public finance. PCAsia designed and delivered training sessions focused on the role of parliaments in climate-informed budget scrutiny and oversight, providing technical guidance on how parliamentary mechanisms can contribute to climate policy accountability and public expenditure tracking.
Integrated approach: to further advance gender and climate integration, PCAsia contributed technical inputs to Asian Forum of Parliamentarians on Population and Development (AFPPD) Regional Workshop on Gender-Responsive Budgeting, where climate change was identified as a cross-cutting factor impacting gender equality. Discussions addressed how parliamentary actors can better integrate gender and climate dimensions into budget policy and oversight practices. The workshop also supported regional dialogue on inclusive budgeting approaches within AIPA frameworks.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
